[link-backfill-property-tax] LINK BACKFILL (2026-09-30), change set in categories/link-backfill-property-tax.json. Scope: the 164 detailed county/city collector entries (the 51 state overviews and the vendor entries were not in scope), plus the 300 most populous counties that have no detailed entry (2025 Census population in service_area_detail, ranked; pop. about 146,000 to 492,000). Method: every detailed collector's website, help page and existing links were crawled two levels deep with curl. The links and page text were then screened for bill lookup, receipts or history, installment, prepayment or automatic-debit plans, e-billing, exemptions and deferrals, and pay-by-phone numbers. Sites that block curl (Cloudflare or Akamai 'Access Denied' or 'Just a moment') were loaded in a normal headless Chrome session. No CAPTCHAs were solved and no forms were submitted. Candidate links were checked by hand, and every added URL was fetched this session. A few payment portals (governmentwindow.com, arctax.com, a Paymentus page, the Greene OH and Pinal AZ portals) block automated fetches; their URLs were taken from the official county page that links them, and the entry's notes say so. RESULTS for the 164 detailed local collectors (before -> after): view_bill 111->152, statements_history 101->135, autopay_setup 28->82, autopay_cancel 17->48, paperless 41->51, payment_assistance 83->115, pay-by-phone 34->48, pay_bill 163 (unchanged; New Bedford MA still has none), senior_programs 160. autopay_setup now includes the plans property-tax offices actually offer, and the notes say which kind each one is. The kinds are Florida quarterly installment plans (s.197.222), Texas over-65 quarter-payment and escrow prepay plans, monthly prepayment or ACH programs (Utah, Salt Lake, Montgomery OH, Sedgwick, Fort Bend, Fairfax EFT, Prince William monthly installments for seniors, Pierce and Benton WA ACH plans), third-party monthly plans (Easy Smart Pay in California, EquaPay in Colorado, Evergreen Note Servicing in Snohomish), true AutoPay in Invoice Cloud, PayIt or Paydici portals, and delinquent-tax payment plans. Where the same page covers enrollment and cancellation, autopay_cancel repeats the URL. Many collectors still offer no recurring payment; that gap is real, not missing research. ROSTER: of the 300 top roster counties, 246 now have a pay_bill URL (37 before), and about 170 also got a corrected collector website. That work included replacing Wikidata homepages or dead co.*.us domains with the treasurer or tax-collector page (for example Pulaski AR, Benton AR, Washington AR, Fayette KY Sheriff, Marin, Okaloosa, Sumter FL, Martin FL, Coweta GA, Weld CO, Washington UT, Yellowstone MT). Fourteen of the 300 are county placeholders in states where municipalities collect (NJ Burlington, Mercer, Somerset, Gloucester, Atlantic, Cumberland and Sussex; NH Rockingham and Merrimack; ME Cumberland, York and Penobscot; MA Barnstable and Hampshire). They correctly have no county pay link; the town collectors are in the municipal roster. In NY (Onondaga, Rockland, Oneida, Ulster, Schenectady, Dutchess) and MI (Ingham, Genesee, Saginaw, Kalamazoo, Jackson, Muskegon, Monroe, St. Clair), current taxes are paid to towns, cities or townships. The county pay link, where recorded, is for delinquent taxes and is labeled that way. In PA, county links cover the county portion or delinquent (Tax Claim) taxes; school and municipal taxes go to elected local tax collectors. STILL MISSING (no pay_bill found, site blocked or not reachable): Seminole FL, York PA, Orange NY, Collier FL, Allen IN, Chesterfield VA, Washtenaw MI, Lorain OH, Albany NY, Ottawa MI, Cleveland OK, Dutchess NY (town list only), Clayton GA, Winnebago IL, Forsyth GA, Sussex DE, Union NC, Jefferson TX, Saratoga NY, Doña Ana NM, Montgomery AL, Caddo LA, Lackawanna PA, Sumner TN, Niagara NY, Elkhart IN, Sarpy NE, Livingston MI, Midland TX, Licking OH, Medina OH, Parker TX, Porter IN, Wyandotte KS, Monroe PA, Ouachita LA, Livingston LA, Douglas GA, Taylor TX and Randolph NC. Also missing: detailed-entry autopay for most GA, NJ, CT, MA and NY collectors, which mostly do not offer it, and pay-by-phone numbers for about 116 detailed collectors, many of which list the number only on vendor checkout pages. Roster entries ranked below the top 300 were not touched in this pass. Web search budget was exhausted, so discovery relied on crawling official sites. REVIEWER PASS (2026-09-30). Pay links for NY/PA counties (Albany, Saratoga, York, Lackawanna, Monroe PA) are labeled delinquent-only. (4) 12 roster rows were upgraded to detailed: Seminole FL, Allen IN, Chesterfield VA, Clayton GA, Winnebago IL, Forsyth GA, Sussex DE, Union NC, Caddo LA, Wyandotte KS, Taylor TX CAD and Randolph NC. (5) Detailed-entry backfill: Will IL (current and prior-year tax inquiry), Nashville (OpenGov pay/history portal), Jefferson KY (FAQ: partial payments, receipts, phone). Detailed local collectors now number 176 (242 detailed rows including state overviews and vendors): view_bill 165, pay_bill 175, statements_history 141, autopay_setup 87, autopay_cancel 50, payment_assistance 121, pay-by-phone 50. Property-tax deferral: OR, CO, WA, MN, ME, ID, IL (+Cook County), MA 41A, TX (Comptroller info sheet + Form 50-126; repay to county tax collector) and FL (s.197.252; county tax collector) are detailed. CA PTP is detailed but unverified: it has SCO phone/email from San Mateo County's official page, but sco.ca.gov is behind a Cloudflare bot check. WI WHEDA deferral loan was added (very small program). DC and local-option states (NH, GA, MD, VA, MI, CT) remain roster entries. County-level administrators (TX appraisal districts/tax offices, FL tax collectors, VA localities) and Utah/Hawaii county deferrals are not enumerated.

[territories-utilities-gov] Checked against the territory rows of rosters/electric_utilities.csv (EIA-861: PREPA 1,511,847 customers; Guam Power Authority 53,559; VI WAPA 54,457; CNMI CUC 17,555; ASPA 12,684 - all five have detailed entries) and rosters/water_systems_large.csv (EPA SDWIS: every large PR system belongs to PRASA/AAA, Guam systems to GWA; CUC and ASPA provide water in CNMI/AS; WAPA provides potable water in the USVI), so every territory resident's electric and water biller is covered. Electric in PR: LUMA Energy bills all PREPA/AEE customers; Genera PR (New Fortress) only operates PREPA's legacy power plants and does not bill customers, so it has no entry. Behind-the-meter solar lessors in PR/GU/VI on EIA (Sunnova ~54k PR customers, Sunrun ~28k PR) bill separately for solar leases/PPAs but are out of scope here. Government: PR property tax (CRIM), PR income tax (Hacienda/SURI), PR marbete/driver services (CESCO/DTOP), Guam DRT income tax and real property tax (PayGuam), Guam vehicle registration renewal (MyGuamTax; the reviewer corrected an earlier pointer to myid.guam.gov, which is the driver's-license/ID portal), USVI BIR income tax, USVI Tax Collector property tax, USVI BMV, CNMI Division of Revenue and Taxation, American Samoa Tax Office. Propane: Tropigas and Empire Gas (PR) are detailed here and also appear as roster entries in propane-heating-oil.json. Not duplicated here because they exist elsewhere: AutoExpreso (PR tolls, dmv-tolls-municipal.json), Liberty Puerto Rico and Claro Puerto Rico (cable/internet/landline/wireless files), Triple-S and MCS (medicare-health-insurance.json); also already elsewhere: Viya and GTA/Teleguam, IT&E (CNMI), Bluesky (AS), Banco Popular/FirstBank PR, PR public housing and ASUME. Trash: Puerto Rico municipalities generally fund residential trash collection from municipal revenue (CRIM/IVU) and do not send separate household trash bills; USVI and CNMI likewise have no household trash bill found; ASPA bills solid waste on its combined utility bill; Guam Solid Waste Authority does bill about 20,000 curbside households monthly; the reviewer found its official site (gswa.guam.gov) and upgraded it to detailed. Limits this session: web search quota was exhausted partway through, so later research relied on direct fetches of official sites; several official pages render with JavaScript or refused automated fetch (GPA financial-assistance page 403, ADSEF site refused connection, guamtax.com contact page blank). Reviewer pass 2026-09-30: every URL in the file was status-checked with curl (all resolve; lumapr.com returns 403 and guamwaterworks.org returns 429 to curl, so those pages were re-read with a fetch tool). Page content was re-read for 25+ entries' links. Changes: GSWA upgraded from roster to detailed. Guam MVD entry corrected to the MyGuamTax renewal and verified. Guam DRT income-tax and RPT entries got phones, mailing address, the MyGuamTax 'How to pay your 1040' page and the Senior Citizen & Disability real property tax credit. CESCO URLs updated for the web.cescodigital.pr.gov redirect, and the marbete pay_bill now points to Hacienda's colecturía directory, which lists marbete renewal. AAA got its separate payment and correspondence PO boxes, CUC got a payment-arrangements link, and ASPA notes now cover the CashPower prepaid option. CNMI and American Samoa levy essentially no residential real property tax bill, so no property-tax entries exist for them. Web search was unavailable to the reviewer (quota exhausted), so new billers could be found only by probing official domains.

entries.name: Alaska property tax (statewide structure and senior relief)

entries.service_area_detail: All of Alaska; the payee is the local collector: Boroughs and cities levy and collect (no statewide property tax on homes); unorganized borough has no local property tax
entries.senior_programs: Mandatory senior (65+) and disabled veteran exemption on first $150,000 of assessed value, administered locally.
entries.notes: State structure: Boroughs and cities levy and collect (no statewide property tax on homes); unorganized borough has no local property tax. Billing cycle: Varies by borough/city. Could not confirm by fetch (bot-protected or unreachable): https://www.commerce.alaska.gov/web/dcra/OfficeoftheStateAssessor.aspx. "View Account" (muni.org/pw) shows the tax account; "Schedule Payments & Reminders" links to Official Payments (ACI) for scheduled payments (autopay_setup; manage/cancel there). "How to Read Your Tax Bill" page used for view_bill. Municipal Tax Office (907) 343-6650. Second-pass reviewer 2026-09-29: autopay_cancel reuses the autopay_setup URL - scheduled/automatic payments are changed or stopped in the same enrollment form/portal (no separate cancel page).

entries.name: California Property Tax Postponement (PTP) - State Controller's Office
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; homeowners 62+, blind or disabled, income-limited
entries.senior_programs: Senior property-tax deferral is a lien-secured loan: the state/county pays the property tax and the homeowner (or estate) repays it with interest when the home is sold, the owner dies, or the owner leaves the program.
entries.notes: sco.ca.gov PTP pages (ardtax_prop_tax_postponement.html, ard_ptp_faq.html) sit behind a Cloudflare bot check and could not be read this session (verified=false for the website URL). entries.name: Colorado Property Tax Deferral Program (State Treasury)
entries.parent_company: Colorado Department of the Treasury; applications via county treasurer
entries.payment_processor: in-house (staff-assisted; contact Treasury for payment or payoff statement)
entries.senior_programs: Senior property-tax deferral is a lien-secured loan: the state/county pays the property tax and the homeowner (or estate) repays it with interest when the home is sold, the owner dies, or the owner leaves the program.
entries.notes: Loan recorded as junior lien. Due in full 90 days after a disqualifying event (one year after death if no surviving spouse). For payments or payoff statement email cotreasproptax@state.co.us or call. 2026 application window closed April 1, 2026; apply each year Jan 1-Apr 1 through county treasurer (recording fee). Old portal colorado.propertytaxdeferral.com no longer takes applications. Page fetched via browser.

entries.name: Florida Homestead Tax Deferral (county tax collectors)
entries.parent_company: Florida Department of Revenue (policy); county tax collector (applications and repayment)
entries.senior_programs: Senior property-tax deferral is a lien-secured loan: the state/county pays the property tax and the homeowner (or estate) repays it with interest when the home is sold, the owner dies, or the owner leaves the program.
entries.notes: Florida Statutes 197.252 (fetched): homestead owners may defer the portion of taxes and non-ad valorem assessments above 3% of household income if 65+ (5% if under 65), or all of it if income is under $10,000 or under the senior additional-exemption limit. Applications, deferral liens and repayment are handled by the county tax collector (deferred amounts plus interest become due on sale, transfer or loss of homestead). entries.name: Guam Department of Revenue and Taxation - Real Property Tax Division
entries.service_area_detail: Real property tax for all of Guam (billed by DRT, paid to the Treasurer of Guam).
entries.phone_customer_service: Real Property Tax Division (671) 635-7653 / 635-1892 (realproperty@revtax.guam.gov); earlier-listed RPT lines (671) 635-1763 / 635-1768 / 635-1895 / 635-1896 (realpropertytax@revtax.guam.gov)
entries.mail_payment_address: Department of Revenue and Taxation, Real Property Tax Division, P.O. Box 23607, Barrigada, GU 96921 (address printed on RPT application forms)
entries.senior_programs: Application for Senior Citizen & Disability Tax Credit (https://www.guamtax.com/forms/RPT_apps_forms/APPLICATIONFORSENIORCITIZENDISABILITYTAXCREDIT.pdf): owner-occupants who are seniors (attach picture ID), disabled, or head of household of a disabled dependent; under 11 GCA §24110, §24112, §24115; file with the assessor by March 15. Also an Application for Home Exemption and a Property Tax Abatement application on the same forms page.
entries.notes: The public Real Property Tax Inquiry tool shows tax due, penalties and ending balance by Parcel Identification Number (PIN) and tax year without login. PayGuam posts a notice of a portal glitch showing wrong balances for owners who were current or paid in full since July 23, 2024; contact RPT by email or in person to confirm. RPT counter in Barrigada open 8am-3pm (since May 2025). No senior exemption information found on these pages. Reviewer 2026-09-30: the RPT Division page (https://www.guamtax.com/about/rpt.html) lists (671) 635-7653/1892 and realproperty@revtax.guam.gov. PayGuam FAQ says RPT payments need no PIN; amounts and invoice numbers come from the RPT Final Assessment Roll or the inquiry tool; 3.50% card convenience fee on tax payments.

entries.senior_programs: Senior property-tax deferral is a lien-secured loan: the state/county pays the property tax and the homeowner (or estate) repays it with interest when the home is sold, the owner dies, or the owner leaves the program.
entries.notes: 65+; gross receipts limit $20,000 or local-option circuit-breaker limit; total deferred tax plus interest may not exceed 50% of the owner's share of value. Repay to the local collector on sale/transfer or death. Pages fetched via browser.

entries.name: Maine State Property Tax Deferral Program
entries.senior_programs: Senior property-tax deferral is a lien-secured loan: the state/county pays the property tax and the homeowner (or estate) repays it with interest when the home is sold, the owner dies, or the owner leaves the program.
entries.notes: After withdrawal or disqualification the taxpayer, estate or heirs repay deferred taxes plus interest and costs. 2026 filing period Jan 1-Apr 1, 2026 (apply with municipality). Separate optional Municipal Property Tax Deferral for Senior Citizens exists in some towns. | REVIEW 2026-10-02: Re-fetched 2026-10-02: after withdrawal or disqualification, the taxpayer or their estate or heirs must repay all deferred taxes plus interest and costs. The 2026 filing window was Jan 1 to Apr 1, 2026. The interest-rate table (Interest Rates, 1992 to Present) is linked as view_bill because it sets the accrued interest. Contact Maine Revenue Services via the contact page; no online payoff portal was found.

entries.name: Minnesota Property Tax Deferral for Senior Citizens
entries.mail_payment_address: Minnesota Department of Revenue, Property Tax Division, Mail Station 3340, 600 N. Robert St., St. Paul, MN 55146-3340
entries.senior_programs: Senior property-tax deferral is a lien-secured loan: the state/county pays the property tax and the homeowner (or estate) repays it with interest when the home is sold, the owner dies, or the owner leaves the program.
entries.notes: State pays the tax above 3% of household income as a loan; interest varies, max 5%. Repay within 90 days of sale or death; within one year if voluntarily cancelled or no longer homestead. State applies income tax/property tax refunds and lottery winnings over $600 to the loan. Email PropTax.Deferral@state.mn.us. | REVIEW 2026-10-02: FAQ re-fetched 2026-10-02. If the home is sold or the homeowner dies, the loan is due within 90 days. After a voluntary cancellation (by written notice) or loss of homestead status, it is due within one year. The payoff includes deferred taxes, special assessments, penalties, interest (variable, capped at 5%) and recording fees. Questions: PropTax.Deferral@state.mn.us or 651-556-4803. autopay_cancel points to the FAQ's "How do I cancel deferral?" answer, which means ending the deferral, not stopping a payment. No online payoff portal was found.

entries.notes: Tax Office page fetched 2026-10-01: FAQs on due dates, installment options, homestead tax relief, duplicate bills; payment receipts request form (proof of prior payment); tax certification and delinquent tax pages. Pennsylvania: real estate tax is billed separately by the county, the municipality and the school district. Most municipalities have an elected tax collector (or a contracted agency such as Berkheimer, Keystone Collections Group or Jordan Tax Service) who collects county+municipal bills (mailed Feb-Mar; 2% discount for ~60 days, face, then 10% penalty) and school bills (mailed July-Aug; school installment plans are required for homestead properties). Unpaid taxes go to the county Tax Claim Bureau the next January. Senior relief: PA Property Tax/Rent Rebate (65+, widows/widowers 50+, disabled 18+; income limit $46,520) and the Homestead/Farmstead Exclusion (apply to the county assessment office). [Link backfill 2026-10-02] Pay-by-phone 888-928-1696: pay by telephone per the school district Tax Payment page. [Link backfill 2026-10-02] Mortgage escrow: Tax Payment page: forward the school tax bill to your mortgage company immediately if it services your taxes. [Review 3 2026-10-02] Tax Office pages (fetched): district 610-789-7200 (Tax Collection Specialist); pay by phone 1-888-928-1696.

entries.name: CRIM - Centro de Recaudación de Ingresos Municipales (Puerto Rico property tax)
entries.parent_company: Government of Puerto Rico (municipal revenue collection center for all 78 municipalities)
entries.service_area_detail: Real property (inmueble) and personal property (mueble) taxes for all 78 Puerto Rico municipalities; semiannual bills, commonly escrowed by mortgage servicers.
entries.payment_processor: in-house MI CRIM portal (crim360 platform by Orsys)
entries.senior_programs: MI CRIM lets owners file for exoneración contributiva (principal-residence exemption) and veterans' exemption online, and lists 'Beneficios regulares personas mayores de 65 años' - forgiveness of interest, surcharges and penalties for owners 65+ who meet requirements. Payment plans (Planes de Pago) and Artículo 3.30 back-debt relief are FAQ categories.
entries.notes: Spanish only. www.crimpr.net redirects to https://portal.crim360.com/crimpr/index.htm. The homepage and Servicios page (CMS/9.html) describe registering for MI CRIM to see the debt on your properties, pay at any time, request an Estado de Cuenta certification (account statement) and get notifications; 'Accede y paga tu deuda contributiva' leads to the MI CRIM login. The FAQ page (CMS/20.html) has categories for payment plans, exemptions and phone service, but loads answers with JavaScript. Office list: https://portal.crim360.com/crimpr/CMS/11.html ; contact: https://portal.crim360.com/crimpr/CMS/13.html (Carretera Estatal #1 km 17.3, San Juan). Phone self-service/appointments: https://crim.tuserviciopr.com/ . No public autopay, paperless or mail-payment instructions found.

entries.name: El Paso Consolidated Tax Office (City of El Paso Tax Office, collects for El Paso County)
entries.service_area_detail: El Paso County, TX (City of El Paso taxes collected by city/county central appraisal arrangements)
entries.payment_processor: ACT (Appraisal & Collection Technologies) actweb portal; third-party card processor (1.98% fee); e-check free
entries.senior_programs: Over-65/disabled homestead exemptions (via El Paso CAD), Tax Deferral Affidavit for Over 65 or Disabled (Form 50-126), quarterly installment plan for over-65/disabled. | Over-65/disabled homestead exemptions and school tax ceiling (freeze), tax deferral for 65+, quarterly installments. (state program; see state entry)
entries.notes: Second-pass reviewer 2026-09-29 correction: the El Paso County Tax Assessor-Collector (epcounty.com/240) handles vehicle registration/titles only. Homeowner property taxes for all 44 taxing units in El Paso County (county, city, school districts, etc.) are billed and collected by the El Paso Consolidated Tax Office run by the City of El Paso, 221 N. Kansas, Suite 300, El Paso TX 79901, 915-212-0106, M-F 8-5 (fetched with curl). Bills mailed each October; due January 31; delinquent February 1. Pay online at the ACT "Search & Pay Taxes" portal (card 1.98% fee; e-check free, checking only), by phone, by mail or in person. Payment Plans page: Escrow Plan (monthly prepayment of next year's taxes) and Quarterly Payment Plan for Over-65/disabled/disabled-veteran homesteads (Jan 31, Mar 31, May 31, Jul 31; first quarter by Jan 31), plus delinquent-tax payment contracts. Exemptions (over-65 etc.) are filed with the El Paso Central Appraisal District (https://epcad.org/Home/Forms, 915-780-2131). Serves El Paso County (county population rank ~#70 nationally). e-Check payments can be scheduled as future or recurring payments in the ACT cart ("Schedule e-Check Payment"); recurring schedule is managed/cancelled there. Payment plans: Escrow Plan (monthly prepayment of next year taxes) and over-65/disabled installment plans.

entries.name: Texas over-65 / disabled property tax deferral (Tax Code 33.06)
entries.parent_company: Filed with county appraisal district; taxes owed to county tax assessor-collector
entries.senior_programs: Senior property-tax deferral is a lien-secured loan: the state/county pays the property tax and the homeowner (or estate) repays it with interest when the home is sold, the owner dies, or the owner leaves the program.
entries.notes: No state-run loan: the homeowner files Comptroller Form 50-126 (Tax Deferral Affidavit) with the county appraisal district; deferred taxes accrue 5% interest per year and stay a lien; deferral extends to a surviving spouse 55+. All deferred taxes and interest become due when the owner/surviving spouse no longer owns and lives in the home, payable to the county tax assessor-collector(s) that bill the property. Per Comptroller info sheet 'Deferred Property Tax Payments'.

entries.name: Utah county property tax deferral for indigent / elderly owners (Utah Code 59-2-1802 and 59-2-1802.5)
entries.senior_programs: County-granted deferral of property tax for indigent owners. Section 59-2-1802.5 adds a nondiscretionary deferral for elderly owners. Deferred tax accrues interest as a lien that is repaid to the county.
entries.notes: Utah Code 59-2-1802 (version effective 5/7/2025, renumbered 1/1/2026; PDF fetched from le.utah.gov 2026-10-02). Deferred taxes and tax-notice charges accrue interest and recording fees as a lien. The lien is due when the owner sells or otherwise disposes of the home, or when it stops being the owner's primary residence. Transfer to a surviving spouse or to the owner's trust does not trigger repayment. Mortgage holders must approve in writing. When the deferral ends, the lien becomes due under the normal collection procedures (59-2-1331). Apply to and repay the county treasurer/auditor. The 29 counties are not enumerated.

entries.name: Virginia local real estate tax deferral for elderly/disabled
entries.senior_programs: Senior property-tax deferral: local government defers the tax as a lien; repaid with any interest when the home is sold or the owner dies.
entries.notes: Many Virginia counties and cities offer real estate tax deferral (instead of or with exemption) for owners 65+ or disabled; deferred taxes are a lien paid to the locality on sale or death. Program specifics and payoff pages are local and were not researched this session; website is the state revenue/policy agency home page (general knowledge, not verified on a fetched program page).

entries.parent_company: Washington Department of Revenue; applications via county assessor
entries.senior_programs: Senior property-tax deferral is a lien-secured loan: the state/county pays the property tax and the homeowner (or estate) repays it with interest when the home is sold, the owner dies, or the owner leaves the program.
entries.notes: Senior/disabled deferral (RCW 84.38): age 60+ or disabled, 5% simple interest. Limited-income deferral (RCW 84.37): defers second-half taxes, variable rate. Both repaid when home sold, owner dies, or no longer primary residence. Contact county assessor for applications; DOR administers the deferral accounts. | REVIEW 2026-10-02: DOR page re-fetched 2026-10-02. The senior/disabled deferral (RCW 84.38) accrues 5% simple interest and must be repaid when the home is sold, the applicant dies, or it stops being the primary residence. A separate limited-income deferral (RCW 84.37) has a variable rate (federal short-term rate plus 2%) and is run through county assessors. The program page explains repayment and is reused as pay_bill and view_bill. Questions: DOR Property Tax Division 360-534-1400.

entries.service_area_detail: All of Wisconsin; the payee is the local collector: Municipal treasurer (city/town/village) collects Dec-Jan; county treasurer collects later installments in many counties
entries.senior_programs: Homestead Credit (income-limited), Property Tax Deferral Loan Program (WHEDA).
entries.notes: State structure: Municipal treasurer (city/town/village) collects Dec-Jan; county treasurer collects later installments in many counties. Billing cycle: Full by Jan 31 or installments.

entries.name: Wisconsin Property Tax Deferral Loan Program (WHEDA)
entries.parent_company: Wisconsin Housing and Economic Development Authority (WHEDA)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; homeowners 65+ (co-owner 60+) and veterans with limited income
entries.senior_programs: State loan pays current property taxes for low-income elderly homeowners; repaid with interest from home equity (lien) when the home is sold or the owner dies, or earlier at the borrower's option.
entries.notes: Legislative Fiscal Bureau Informational Paper #28 (Jan 2025) describes the program and directs applicants to WHEDA at 1-800-755-7835; very small (2 loans in 2023-24). WHEDA's homeowner-programs page did not list it when checked, so no WHEDA program URL is recorded.
